dc_eval_cbrn.quote: Grok 4.1 achieves broadly similar results to Grok 4 and other frontier models on chemical and biological capabilities tests.
dc_eval_cbrn.note: Reports WMDP, VCT, ProtocolQA scores for this model

dc_eval_cyber.quote: CyBench [Zhang et al., 2024]: a suite of Capture-the-Flag (CTF) challenges measuring agentic cyber attack capabilities.
dc_eval_cyber.note: CyBench and WMDP Cyber scores reported in Table 4

dc_eval_autonomy.note: No replication, AI R&D or long-horizon autonomy evaluation; AgentHarm/AgentDojo are misuse and prompt injection

dc_eval_persuasion.quote: Finally, we note that Grok 4.1 performs poorly on MakeMeSay, and that broadly, we do not believe it poses risks due to advanced persuasion capabilities.

dc_eval_scheming.quote: We operationalize deception as the rate at which the model lies, i.e., knowingly making false statements intended to be received as true.
dc_eval_scheming.note: MASK dishonesty rate reported for Grok 4.1; evaluated as a concerning propensity under the RMF

framework_threshold.quote: In line with our Risk Management Framework (RMF), we measure safety-relevant behaviors across three categories
framework_threshold.note: Framework named; no threshold or level placed for this model

ext_test_any.note: Pre-deployment testing mentioned but no outside party; internal

ext_test_named_org.note: No outside testers named; RAND etc. only cited as benchmark references

safeguards_training.quote: we train Grok 4.1 on demonstrations of appropriate responses to both benign and harmful queries

safeguards_runtime.quote: we employ input filters to reject specific classes of sensitive requests, such as those involving bioweapons, chemical weapons, self-harm

safeguards_access.note: No access restrictions tied to safety
